A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniSVG and MMSVG-2M. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support comparison despite substantial evaluation and presentation revisions.

before.justification: v2 reports original SVG-generation comparisons, parameterization and architecture ablations, character-reference results and a user study.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark comparisons, ablations and user-study outcomes, alongside retained qualitative generation results.

M1.justification: The tokenizer, Qwen2.5-VL backbones and training objective remain unchanged; the 4B/8B labels do not establish an architecture change. However, v3 Table 7 replaces the two-image character-reference instruction with a single-image instruction, while Section A.2 still specifies two images. Whether the actual conditioning procedure changed is unresolved.

E1.justification: The main evaluation changes from MMSVG-2M icons, illustrations and characters to GPT-4o-generated icon and illustration inputs. Comparative character coverage disappears from the main results and comparison figures. Character data remain in training and qualitative demonstrations, so character generation itself is retained.

E2.justification: VTracer becomes an evaluated image-to-SVG comparator in v3 Table 2; v2 used it for dataset construction without reporting comparison scores. The other principal text-to-SVG and image-to-SVG comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v3 Section 3.2 introduces GPT-4o benchmark construction with 150 text prompts per icon/illustration subset and 150 additional descriptions for image generation. The dataset table replaces separate test counts with larger validation counts. The user study changes from five text and three image prompts to 150 of each, with 15 participants disclosed. Generation-time evaluation is removed; the new study's one-tenth sampling description remains unclear.

E4.justification: The natural-image failure case study illustrated in v2 Figure 9 is removed, although its textual limitation remains. Parameterization, model-scaling, vision-backbone and FLUX-Redux downsampling analyses are retained, including material relocated to the appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run/seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The dataset's token-length spread summaries are retained; the newly disclosed participant count concerns study sample size.

E6.justification: Main comparison, ablation and user-study scores are extensively revised. Illustration FID changes from OmniSVG(7B) 66.91 versus IconShop 84.04 in v2 Table 3 to OmniSVG-L(8B) 138.42 versus IconShop 107.93 in v3 Table 2. This reverses their reported ranking under changed benchmark inputs, not establishing a same-setting regression. Character comparison scores, timing results and the approximately 7-point character-reference alignment result are removed.

T1.justification: The SVG/path definitions, coordinate-token mapping and next-token prediction objective in Equation 1 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central OmniSVG, MMSVG-2M and professional-workflow contributions remain. The introduction narrows its advertised MMSVG-Bench scope from three tasks to text-to-SVG and image-to-SVG, although character-reference capability and task descriptions persist elsewhere.

C2.justification: v3 motivates generated benchmark inputs as avoiding excessive training/test similarity. Section 5.2 shifts from across-metric text-generation superiority toward competitive quality and shorter output sequences. The natural-image and generation-time limitations remain, while the explicit multi-image-encoder advantage and stylization future direction are omitted.

D1.justification: v3 adds direct dataset, benchmark, model and code links and identifies Fudan's CFFF computing platform. Training and sampling settings are relocated unchanged to Appendix B.2. Some previously specified ablation-dataset and user-study shuffling details are no longer documented.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Log-linear Attention and Transformers Are RNNs, removes Step1X-3D and stylization references, and expands discussion of VTracer. Positioning relative to StarVector, LLM4SVG and other SVG generators remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially condensed and rewritten. Scaling, implementation information and lengthy baseline discussions move into reorganized Appendices B–D, and references move before the appendices. The abstract, terminology and model labels also receive edits.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a predominantly single-column conference format. Main qualitative comparison panels are replaced, the results table loses its timing column and character block, and the instruction display is redesigned. Retained training curves and the generation gallery move to the appendices; the failure-case figure disappears.

improvement.justification: v3 improves comparison breadth through VTracer, documents generated benchmark construction and supplies direct resource links. However, it removes v2's quantitative character and runtime evidence supporting central claims. Its claimed FID superiority conflicts with the illustration ranking in Table 2, and the revised user-study sampling counts are unclear. These benefits and losses leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
